fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses HfNbTiVAl10 rather than the target Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W design space and therefore misses the material system and principal baseline.

It replaces the target composition-screening intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation, VEC/density screening of 38,326 compositions, and selection of Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5—with an unrelated imaging-driven neural-network proposal.
It specifies tensile testing and fracture toughness, whereas the demonstrated target result was room-temperature quasi-static compression and compressive fracture strain in an as-cast alloy.

It omits the central target mechanism: reduced VEC lowering the Peierls–Nabarro barrier, improving dislocation mobility and slip, and delaying brittle cracking while retaining relatively high modulus.
The claimed 30–50% accuracy improvement and tenfold efficiency gain are unsupported by the cited evidence.
Neither cited paper validates physics-informed microstructure-based machine learning, fracture-toughness prediction, or the proposed method for HfNbTiVAl10.
explanation: The response is testable in a general sense but does not reconstruct the target study. It identifies neither equimolar as-cast NbMoTaVW as the brittle baseline nor Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 as the screened low-VEC alloy, and it misses the actual conditions and outcomes: room-temperature compression at 5 × 10^-4 s^-1, 1115 ± 18 MPa yield strength, 35.7 ± 0.9% fracture strain, and 2550 ± 75 MPa compressive strength. Its proposed blinded benchmark has explicit error thresholds, which gives it some discriminability, but it lacks sample-size and held-out-processing specifications and compares unlike computational workflows. The ±10% microstructure boundary is arbitrary and incomplete for flaw-sensitive toughness. Most importantly, the supplied evidence concerns mechanical behavior and processing of other refractory HEAs and does not support the asserted machine-learning accuracy or efficiency gains, so the proposal remains unsupported rather than a well-evidenced alternative.
